source: VVOB Cambodia / MAFF Kampong Thom Provincial Department of Agriculture — IPM and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Rice, 9-point training presentation, presenter Mr. Tem Seng, Oct 5, 2010 (training slide deck; no elibrary URL visible)
text: For raising rice seedlings, choose a plot with soil free of clumps, well-drained, and reasonably level, using organic manure or ash as a base amendment (សាបប្រើថ្នាលគោក ដីមានមេមោក សំណាបថ្លាសល្អ). Soak and pre-germinate seed for about 7-10 days before sowing on the bed. As a general guide, around 200 g of pure seed is sown per 100 m² of nursery bed. Nursery beds are typically made 1-1.5 m wide, with length depending on the plot's shape and available space. A light starter dose of urea, roughly 0.1 kg (about one handful) per 1 m² of bed, is applied to encourage vigorous seedling growth — treat this as an illustrative rate rather than an exact prescription, since soil fertility varies by field. As a rule of thumb, producing seedlings for 1 hectare of transplanted rice requires about 150-200 m² of nursery bed area and roughly 10-15 kg of seed.
